_provenance.note: Wisconsin dated facts. The most significant underlying finding is NOT itself expressible as a future-expiring citation: Wisconsin's own FoodShare handbook (as of Release 26-01) has not yet been updated to reflect the federal OBBBA ABAWD age expansion (18-64), even though the state's own documented rulemaking deadline for doing so (June 1, 2026) has already passed as of this pack's build date. Because pack-freshness.test.ts fails the build on any ALREADY-past 'expires' date (by design — it is a drift detector, not a fits-every-shape mechanism), that finding is instead the load-bearing warning embedded directly in the abawd-work-requirement supplement text and PROVENANCE.md. The entry below is a genuine forward-looking recheck date (the next handbook release is likely on Wisconsin's annual COLA cadence), not a claim that the age-band conflict itself has a future resolution date.

entries.warning: As of this pack's build date, Wisconsin's own FoodShare handbook (FSH 3.17.1.1, Release 26-01) still states the ABAWD age range as 18-54 (2023 Fiscal Responsibility Act), NOT the federal OBBBA 18-64 band every other state pack in this roster reflects — see the abawd-work-requirement supplement and PROVENANCE.md for the full finding. Wisconsin's likely next handbook release lands on the annual October COLA cycle — re-check FSH 3.17.1 directly for an updated release after this date, and do not assume the state text has caught up to federal law just because this specific recheck window passed without a fresh fetch.

Wisconsin's fixed statewide ABAWD 36-month window (January 1, 2025 – December 31, 2027) expires — the next window begins January 1, 2028 (FSH 3.17.1.7). Do not describe the 2025-2027 window as current after that date.

Wisconsin's SNAP standard deduction ($209/$223/$261/$299 by household-size band), 7-tier utility allowance ladder (HSUA $553 / LUA $385 / EUA $155 / WUA $106 / FUA $48 / PUA $31 / TUA $28), and excess-shelter-deduction cap for non-EBD households ($744) — all set under FSH 8.1.3, effective 10/1/2025 — track the federal FFY26 COLA cycle and are due for the October 2026 update. Find the successor FSH 8.1.3 release before quoting any of these figures after this date.
